body: @zzo / @juliemr could you take a look at this one please?

This issue is this:
https://github.com/isaacs/node-glob/issues/78
karma is using an old version of glob whose async performance is bad.  Just using glob.sync instead increases performance 2x with the same version of glob.  
Using the latest version of glob performance is order of magnitude improved.
Hope to have a fix one way or another soon.

A quick grep:

``` shell
$ grep "glob(" -r node_modules/ --exclude-dir=glob | grep broc | grep '\.js'
node_modules//broccoli/node_modules/rimraf/rimraf.js:    glob(p, globOpts, afterGlob)
node_modules//broccoli-funnel/node_modules/broccoli-read-compat/node_modules/rimraf/rimraf.js:    glob(p, globOpts, afterGlob)
node_modules//broccoli-stew/node_modules/broccoli-funnel/node_modules/rimraf/rimraf.js:    glob(p, globOpts, afterGlob)
node_modules//broccoli-stew/node_modules/fs-extra/node_modules/rimraf/rimraf.js:    glob(p, globOpts, afterGlob)
```

It doesn't look like any of the angular build tools are using async glob directly (is there info on where it's coming from?)

@caitp, it's used by karma's dart plugin.

it's coming from karma which uses (an older version) of glob.  This is about karma taking a long time to run/re-run tests - glob is globbing over 4k files and it's taking a long time.

fwiw it's karma itself that's doing the globbing and taking a long time not the dart plugin - since we're using Dartium no dart2js is happening so the dart plugin isn't doing anything expensive in this case.

really? then I would expect the issue to affect the js tests as well. There
is a small delay, in js, but it's nowhere as significant as the dart. Is it
because the dart dist tree contains many more files?

Hmm, looking at the analysis pointing to node-glob as a culprit, I wonder why we start to see this issue only now, after migration to Brocolli. It used to be very fast with the Gulp-based build.

Back in the old pre-broccoli days karma watched the filesystem itself so it did not have to run full globs whenever a file changed.  Now with broccoli watching the fs - karma gets kicked off fresh for every file change so it must glob over the entire fs each time looking for files (and there are a lot of them).

Oh, I didn't realise that now we've got broccoli _and_ Karma doing the watching... I guess it was done like this to have only one thing in charge of the build, right? Instead of having a separate broccoli and Karma adapter? Hm, but then again, why don't we see the same pb in JS?

karma is no longer doing any watching - only broccoli.  When broccoli detects a change it kicks off a single run from karma.
Haven't looked at the JS stuff yet so don't know about that - will take a look

This started happening only recently. I wonder if it's because of the
generated files that we now have in dart. Maybe part of the solution would
be to make the file patterns more restrictive so that karma doesn't need to
do so much work?

Also, the build could generate a list of changed files so that karma can
use those to figure out which paths to invalidate. But as far as I know,
when we run in dartium the http caching is disabled because the file urls
can't be amended with versioning info.

Ok some bad news - the newer globs don't automatically follow symlinks so they were running much faster :)
So using the latest 'glob' and using sync vs. async glob'ing the we get from ~30 seconds currently to ~20 seconds - faster but not instantaneous.
The heavy hitter is this pattern in karma-dart conf: 'dist/dart/**' which matches ~82k files and takes about 8 seconds just for the glob. 
So yes any way we can make that list of files smaller will help.
